title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and executed a paired experiment to test whether inserting an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial generation policy on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), every produced candidate was accepted by the verifier in both conditions (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We publish the full preregistration and execution bundle (responses, call traces, scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose why the ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates), and give artifact-backed prescriptions (independent generation per condition, adversarial temporal invariants, multi-verifier matrices, canary reachability tests, multi-model comparisons) for future verifier evaluations designed to produce informative discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Operational context and question. Translating operator intent (natural language) into low-level device configuration is central to NetOps automation. A common safety architecture is: generate candidate configuration (LLM) → deterministic verifier → enact or block/rollback. We asked, and preregistered, a confirmatory paired test: does inserting an automated verifier that blocks verifier-detected violations reduce unsafe enactments versus an LLM-only pipeline? (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001). Contribution summary. We (1) provide the frozen preregistration and full, hashed execution artifacts; (2) report exact, preregistered quantitative outcomes (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]); and (3) diagnose—using archived traces—why the run produced a deterministic ceiling and give concrete, artifact-grounded prescriptions for future informative evaluations. Unambiguous study outcome. The preregistered confirmatory hypotheses (H1/H2) were not testable in this execution because every produced candidate was accepted by the verifier in both pipelines (no discordant pairs). We state this explicitly to avoid misinterpretation: this run produced no empirical evidence for or against verifier benefit under its executed design.
sections.related_work: Verifier-assisted NetOps, intent→configuration, and generate–validate–repair architectures motivated our design. Representative verified sources include Aether (agentic AI + digital twin for validation), surveys advocating workflow-centred evaluation for agentic NetOps, and constraint/adaptation approaches such as MeshAgent and generate–validate–repair program-repair literature. These works guided our preregistration (estimands, strata, verifier semantics) and the selection of validator predicates used in scoring. We verify and reference the primary sources used for framing in the artifact bundle (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and freeze. The study preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) was frozen prior to execution (preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04) and contains the verbatim master prompt and the complete experimental plan (estimands, power plan, strata, stopping rules, retry policy, contamination plan). Design and sampling. Paired binary design: 150 confirmatory tasks stratified equally across three ambiguity strata (benign, ambiguous, partially-specified; 50 tasks/stratum) with paired execution under two conditions: (A) baseline (LLM-only generation + enact) and (B) guarded (LLM generation + verifier block-on-violation). Planned episodes = 300. Model, generation policy, and call budget. Executed model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Preregistered generation policy for this run: shared_initial_candidate — one model call per task shared across both conditions (this is critical to the observed ceiling; the exact policy is archived in execution/model_configuration.json). The run used 150 model calls (one per task) as recorded in the execution manifest. Verifier and scoring. The automated verifier/scorer was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain a comprehensive validator_trace per episode (final_configuration, validation_before/after, violation_count, difficulty.pattern, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scorable success was defined exactly as validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true && validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count == 0. Analysis plan (preregistered). Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Primary test: paired McNemar exact test. Confidence: paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729. Multiplicity control: Bonferroni for two confirmatory hypotheses (H1, H2). Contamination, exclusion, and retry rules. Automatic exclusion rules (non-RFC1918 addresses, detected organization names, parser failures) and a retry policy (up to 3 retries for transient provider/infrastructure failures) were preregistered and executed; see execution manifest for per-episode outcomes and hashes.

sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling. Two deterministic, archived facts jointly explain the null discordance: (1) shared_initial generation policy: this run used a single model call per task that was shared between baseline and guarded conditions; identical response SHA256 values across conditions (see representative response SHA256s above) confirm both pipelines received identical candidates. (2) verifier acceptance predicates: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted every generated candidate across all episodes (validation_after.violation_count == 0 in every execution/scoring JSON). Because the guarded pipeline only blocks verifier-rejected candidates, the absence of any rejected candidates produced zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0) and thus no inferential signal about verifier benefit. Scientific interpretation and correct claim. The appropriate, artifact-backed scientific claim is narrow and negative in scope: under the executed design (shared_initial generation, single-call budget, verifier semantics as archived), the experiment produced no evidence for or against verifier utility because it produced no discordant outcomes. It does not prove verifiers are ineffective. Design prescriptions (artifact-grounded) for future informative evaluations. Based on the archived traces and the reproducible failure mode, we make concrete recommendations implementable using the current artifact bundle: (A) Independent per-condition generation: induce non-deterministic candidate diversity by allocating one independent model call per pipeline per task (avoid shared_initial semantics). (B) Adversarial temporal/stateful templates: synthesize confirmatory tasks exercising temporal invariants and multi-step state transitions; the difficulty.pattern taxonomy observed in scoring JSONs provides concrete templates (e.g., "shutdown_configure_restore", "make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change"). (C) Multi-verifier matrix: combine syntactic validators with header-space/reachability checks and SMT-based invariants to broaden violation sensitivity. (D) Canary reachability/emulation: instrument canary endpoints and measure end-to-end service impact and rollback effectiveness (required for H2). (E) Multi-model comparisons and larger per-task budgets: include multiple LLMs and allow multiple independent generations/repairs to expose model-specific fragility. Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial policy and single-generation budget are the primary internal threats. Construct validity: the validator enforced syntactic and command-count predicates but the run did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini) and single-verifier limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the deterministic ceiling prevents confirmatory inference; we therefore avoid claiming equivalence.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to evaluate verifier benefit in an LLM-based intent→configuration pipeline and fully archived the execution. The run completed as planned but produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates across both pipelines for all 150 confirmatory tasks (n11=150), producing a deterministic ceiling that rendered the preregistered confirmatory tests uninformative. The manuscript's value is artifact-centred: (1) it publishes the frozen preregistration and a complete, hashed execution bundle for reproducibility; (2) it provides an artifact-grounded diagnosis of why the ceiling occurred; and (3) it gives concrete, implementable design corrections to produce informative, verifier-sensitive discordant outcomes in future work. We release the full SHA256 manifest and representative artifact pointers so others can reproduce the run and implement corrected confirmatory designs.

limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced verifier-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator construct limits: the validator enforces syntactic and per-command predicates (violation_count, required_command_count, parsed_command_count) visible in scoring JSONs, but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
